chunks: And it is narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:

I sold in al-Madīnah a Harawī sack, each garment for such-and-such a price. They took it and divided it among themselves. Then they found a defect in one garment in it, so they returned it to me. I said to them: I will give you its price for which I sold it to you. They said: No, rather we will take its value from you. So I mentioned that to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: That is binding upon them.

key_terms.ثَمَنَهُ: its sale price agreed upon in the transaction
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a garment or piece of cloth
key_terms.جِرَابًا: a sack or bundle containing goods for sale
key_terms.عَيْبًا: a defect or flaw in the sold item
key_terms.قِيمَتَهُ: its value, meaning its appraised worth
key_terms.هَرَوِيًّا: of Harawī origin; describing the type or provenance of the sack
key_terms.يَلْزَمُهُمْ: it is binding upon them; they are legally obligated

ai.seo_question: If buyers find a defect in one item after dividing purchased goods, are they entitled to the item's market value or only its sale price?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a commercial dispute involving defective goods after a bulk sale had been divided among buyers. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules that the buyers are bound to accept the sale price of the defective item rather than demand its assessed market value.
